text.p: Pen pictures of the probable Sampdoria team for Sunday's serie A clash with Milan:

Fabrizio Ferron, goalkeeper, 31. Started career with Milan youth team in 1984 but never played senior match. Spent eight seasons with Atalanta building reputation as best goalkeeper in serie A never to win international cap. Joined Sampdoria last summer. Missed last two matches, due to return against old club.

David Balleri, defender, 27. Signed from Parma, this powerful, attacking right-back is in second season with Samp. Holds unenviable record of worst discipline record in serie A. Two red cards and 10 bookings in first 13 games. Ordered to clean up game or risk relegation to subs' bench.

Alberigo Evani, defender, 34. Joined in 1993 after spending 13 successful years with Milan. Versatile midfielder who played in Italy team in 1994 World Cup finals, Evani is now part-time defender. Five matches this season. Will retire at end of season to coach Milan's youth team.

Moreno Mannini, defender, 34. Veteran defender in 13th successive season with Sampdoria, Mannini was left-back in league title winning team. Shifted to centre-half in 1995 to replace Pietro Vierchowod. Given vote of confidence last summer when club extended his contract to 2000.

Sinisa Mihajlovic, defender, 27. Won European Cup with Red Star Belgrade in 1991 at age 21 before spending two seasons at Roma. Moved to Samp in 1994 and won Italian Cup. Ex-midfielder, now one of most accomplished sweepers in serie A. Free-kick specialist - witness goal against Milan in 1995 Supercup final.

Oumar Djeng, defender, 24. Rare Samp mistake on transfer market. Bought from Paris St Germain side that won 1996 European Cup Winner's Cup, this Senegal-born Frenchman has failed to earn first-team place. One full match -- 2-1 victory over Milan in Genoa earlier in season.

Emanuele Pesaresi, defender, 20. Joined Sampdoria on loan from Ancona in 1995 but form suffered demands of military service. Started current season on subs' bench but brought in to replace ageing Evani at left-back. Never looked back. Solid in defence, fleet-footed in attack.

Pierre Laigle, midfielder, 27. Sampdoria signed this uncompromising ball-winner from Lens. Superb athlete with good tactical sense, Laigle's performances won him recent debut in French national team. Shy, unassuming character.

Stefano Sacchetti, defender, 24. Lost automatic centre-half role this season for first time since joining from Modena in 1992. Reliable substitute for Mannini in recent matches but reportedly at odds with manager Sven Goran Eriksson over back-up status.

Christian Karembeu, midfielder, 26. New Caledonia-born French international, joined from Nantes in 1995. Won comparisons with Ruud Gullit for dreadlocks and outspoken politics. Opposition to French nuclear tests in Pacific inspired "Samp for Peace" slogan on team shirts. "Wild Dog" has fallen out of favour after transfer tussle between Real Madrid and Barcelona - Karembeu favours Real, but Barca are offering Samp more money. Dropped recently as form suffered.

Marco Franceschetti, midfielder, 30. Started career with Milan in 1985 as midfielder but made breakthrough in 1991 as sweeper with Padua. Joined Sampdoria last season only to request transfer after failing to convince as libero. Now robust ballwinner, Eriksson's answer to Milan's Marcel Desailly.

Fausto Salsano, midfielder, 34. Genoa's answer to Gianfranco Zola, this gifted playmaker is now in 19th serie A season of which 13 in Sampdoria colours. Just missed winning 1990/91 league title, leaving Samp for three-year spell with Roma in summer of 1990. Regular on substitute bench.

Juan Sebastian Veron, midfielder, 21. Talented son of Juan Ramon Veron, three times Intercontinental Cup finalist for Argentina's Estudiantes in 1970s, Veron joined from Boca Juniores last summer. Likened to Cerezo, stylish Brazilian star of Samp's league title team. Tipped by Maradona as future star.

Giovanni Invernizzi, midfielder, 33. Long-serving player and another survivor from Samp's title winning team when ball-winning qualities brought iron to light-weight midfield and kept Russian talent Alexi Mikhaijlichenko on the subs' bench.

Roberto Mancini, striker, 32. Symbol of Sampdoria's "Golden Era", Mancini was bought from Bologna in 1982 to form prolific "terrible twins" partnership with Gianluca Vialli. Despite 139 career goals, highest in serie A, better known as goal-maker, although 12 goals this season have boosted chances of recall to national side. Samp looked like loosing their longest serving player earlier this season to Inter until move vetoed by club.

Vincenzo Montella, striker, 22. Signed from Samp's arch-rivals Genoa in close season after 21 goals in serie B. Injury-hit start to season before confirming reputation as natural goal predator - most of his goals come from inside six-yard box - with 12 goals in as many matches.

Marco Carparelli, striker, 20. Local boy made good. Reared in Samp youth system but destined for third division last summer until pleaded for place on first-team roster. Rewarded with debut in 4-1 win at Roma and four goals in 10 matches. Natural centre-forward - idol was Van Basten - but plays on right wing. Still lives with parents, despite 180km round trip to training.

Vincenzo Iacopino, striker, 20. Another homegrown talent who learnt his football with Ventamiglia on the Italian Riviera before signing for Samp at age 15. Debut performances last season attracted Milan's interest. Lost place to Carparelli due to knee injury. Left-footed, striking turn of pace.
